name: 祇園京都ラーメン (Gion Kyoto Ramen)

claims.text: The house bowl is a soy-sauce (shoyu) ramen; Japanese soy sauce typically contains wheat, and the noodles are wheat-based.
Broths are pork/back-fat (shoyu bowl) and chicken (鶏どろ bowl); shared pots and counter make a vegan meal impractical.

name: 本家 第一旭 本店 (Honke Daiichi Asahi Honten)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles (blended-flour, dried-aged) are the base of every bowl, with a wheat-based soy-sauce tare and gyoza on the menu — a high-gluten kitchen with no gluten-free provision.
The tare is made with raw Kyoto soy sauce (生醤油, Fushimi / Goko Shoyu), which is wheat-fermented; it flavors the broth of the standard bowls.
All bowls are pork-bone broth with char siu and pork fat; no plant-based broth is prepared, so vegan separation is not possible.

name: 本家 第一旭 たかばし本店 (Honke Daiichi Asahi Takabashi Honten)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water and served in a pork-bone broth seasoned with wheat-based soy-sauce tare — no separation from gluten is possible.
The tare uses additive-free raw soy sauce (nama-shoyu) from Fushimi, Kyoto, which is brewed from wheat and soybeans — it contains gluten.
The base broth is pork-bone (chintan) for every bowl, including the no-chashu 'vegetable' ramen, so no bowl is free of animal product.
Many free customizations (noodle firmness, broth richness, soy intensity, chashu lean/fatty, extra negi and bean sprouts) let diners adjust a bowl, though none remove the core wheat/pork allergens.
The signature カラシソバ is dressed with a mustard-vinegar-soy-sauce blend; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so the sauce as well as the noodles carry gluten.
Core bowls are wheat-noodle ramen in pork/chicken and fish-dashi broths; no gluten-free noodles or gluten-free menu are offered, so the kitchen is wheat-heavy and not celiac-appropriate.
Even the plant-leaning soy milk yuzu bowl is finished with roasted bacon, and broths are animal-based; no vegan preparation is described.

name: 家系ラーメン斎藤家 一乗寺店 (Iekei Ramen Saitoya Ichijoji)

claims.text: Wheat noodles (Sakai Seimen) and a wheat-based shoyu tare are core to every bowl; there is no gluten-free preparation and no separate handling, so cross-contamination is unavoidable.
The tare is a soy-sauce base, which in iekei ramen is standard wheat-containing shoyu; reviewers specifically praised the soy-sauce flavor of the broth.
Broth is pork-bone and chicken-oil based with pork chashu and egg; all bowls are animal-based with no vegan option.
The J-mazesoba is dressed in a sweet soy-sauce base, which in standard ramen tare is wheat-containing shoyu; no wheat-free tare is indicated.
All bowls are based on pork-bone and fish broth with meat and egg toppings, so the kitchen is not set up for plant-based diners.

name: 熟成麺屋 神来 西院本店 (Jukusei Menya Jinrai Saiin Honten)

claims.text: The ramen is a soy-sauce-based (醤油ベース) bowl on custom wheat noodles; soy-sauce tare of this style is virtually always made with wheat-containing shoyu.
All ramen is built on chicken-and-pork-bone broth with back-fat, pork chashu, and menma — no plant-based broth is offered or separated.
